metrics.onset_branch_status: continuous-spectrum-blocked at low alpha (rel-err not meaningful)
metrics.headline: first mode resolvable over 14% of cutoff branch, agrees to 1% there; low-alpha onset CS-blocked

verdict_reason: Re-judged with the discrete-mode extractor (eigenfunction-decay + y_max-stationarity). M2 has only a first mode (no second/Mack mode at this Mach). The weak low-Mach 2D first mode sits at the edge of the slow-acoustic continuous spectrum (c_r<=1-1/M), so pyMack can cleanly isolate a discrete mode over only part of Ozgen's lobe (higher-alpha / nose region); the low-alpha onset tail is continuous-spectrum-blocked and cannot be traced as a clean curve. Where pyMack DOES resolve the discrete first mode it agrees with Ozgen (cutoff branch median 1% over 13/93 in-range points; c_i and phase speed consistent with the paper). Conventions/conditions verified-matched to Ozgen (L*=sqrt(nu_e x/U_e), R_L=sqrt(Re_x), alpha_L, c_i=Im(c) temporal, adiabatic wall, Te=288 K). Old verdict ('disagrees') was a mis-digitized-reference + c_r-band-classifier artifact. Honest verdict: 'acceptable' -- first-mode physics verified where resolvable; full-curve extraction continuous-spectrum-limited (a documented compressible-LST numerical isolation limit, not a physics disagreement).
pymack_provenance: c_i grid verification/neutralCurve_verification/_ozgen_compute/ozgen_combined_ci_grid.csv (24x30 mesh, log-spaced Re x linear alpha), from scripts/make_ozgen_fig3_overlay.py (solve_temporal_ozgen_2d, L* scale, classified TS/Mack modes); per-Mach slice copied to verification/neutralCurve_verification/ozgen_m2/pymack_ozgen_M2_ci_grid.csv. Neutral alpha located by bilinear (log-Re) zero-crossing of c_i along alpha at each digitized Re, matched to the NEAREST crossing (headline metric); lower/upper branch-labelled crossings reported as diagnostics.
